question.text: Three particles each of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, are located at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The speed at which they must move to revolve in a circular orbit, under the influence of mutual gravitational force, circumscribing and preserving the equilateral triangle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><msqrt><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></msqrt></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is

solution.text:
The net gravitational force on any particle due to the other two is
Fg=2Gm2a2cos30°=3Gm2a2
Now, r=a3

For circular motion,

Fg=3Gm2a2=mv2r

Solving it we obtain,
v=0.50G
